_comment: Ownership metadata for the RAM inventory. This is DATA, deliberately:
a claim about who owns a buffer, when it is alive and what evidence sets
its size is reviewable in a diff here, instead of being re-derived from
prose in a comment every time someone asks.
'evidence' is the field that matters. 'NOT MEASURED' is the honest value
for anything whose size was chosen rather than derived, and the report
lists every large allocation still carrying it. Do not write a number
into this field that is not traceable to a measurement or to

g_stem_sector_bufs.lifetime: whole session; filled by streamer_thread, drained by audio_thread
g_stem_sector_bufs.overlaps: loop pins (both live while a loop runs)
g_stem_sector_bufs.evidence: depth 12 predates st_latency.h and was chosen against a since-disproven claim that 11 sectors cover the driver's 80 ms allowance. Required read-ahead per st_latency.h is ST_LAT_READAHEAD_SECTORS. OVERSIZED, pending the unified-cache rework.

g_stem_loop_pin_bufs.lifetime: filled when the PLAY gesture arms; released when the loop ends
g_stem_loop_pin_bufs.overlaps: read-ahead ring (both live while a loop runs); dead during idle, transfer and non-loop playback
g_stem_loop_pin_bufs.evidence: ST_LAT_RESIDENCY_SECTORS per region, derived from st_latency.h's guarantee. st17 shipped 3 per region against a wrong 10.15 ms bound; corrected here.

s_v11_verify_scratch.lifetime: one sector verify inside a transfer
s_v11_verify_scratch.overlaps: MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with playback: entering transfer mode sets g_xfer_mode (streamer stops prefetching) and g_playing=0 (audio thread stops rendering the stem path).
s_v11_verify_scratch.evidence: one sector, fixed by ST11_SECTOR_BYTES; the question is not its size but whether it needs to be its own allocation. ALIASING WAS ATTEMPTED IN THE MEMORY-CLEANUP COMMIT AND WITHDRAWN, deliberately. Overlaying it on the sector pool is sound on the two ends that stop (producer and consumer both quiesce, and a two-block barrier makes the consumer's stop provable rather than probable) but NOT on what is left behind: st_stream_stop() does not clear ready_sector, and the SPSC mailbox may still publish a slot whose bytes the transfer overwrote. Fixing that needs a way to say 'nothing in this ring is resident any more', and the mailbox API cannot say it: st_stem_mbox_init() is documented as requiring a quiescent ring AND as asserting that one named sector is ALREADY resident and adopted -- which is precisely the claim that is false after a transfer has written over the pool. Making it true again means re-reading that sector synchronously, i.e. rebuilding the boot/reload sequence at every transfer exit. The unified sector cache carries per-slot validity, so 'void' is a state it can already represent, and the reclamation moves there rather than shipping a stale-sector race for 8192 bytes.

g_meta.phases: loaded at boot, mutated by control paths whose audio effect is unreachable

mix32.phases: none reachable with a Stem Tape song selected

trk.owner: inherited per-track state; Stem Tape reads vol/mute/solo from it
trk.evidence: partially live: Stem Tape genuinely uses vol_q8/muted/solo. The rest is classic.

g_stem_fx.phases: FX overlay open, and the bounded echo tail after it closes
g_stem_fx.overlaps: none. ONE rack exists: STEM scope points it at a stem, GLOBAL scope inserts it after the mix. Moving the target moves this instance rather than creating another, which is the whole reason there is no per-stem array here.
g_stem_fx.evidence: 32,768 B of it is the echo delay line, sized by .github/scripts/stemtape_fx_budget.py: 0.375 beat (banks.ts:460 ratios[2] at the committed default macro 0.5) at the 66 BPM admitted floor, Q15 mono, rounded to a power of two so the 48 kHz loop masks instead of dividing. The remaining ~184 B is filter/distortion/gate/echo state plus four engage ramps. A stereo line would be 65,536 B and was rejected.
